newsitem.title: USA: House votes higher interest rates on disaster loan.
newsitem.headline: House votes higher interest rates on disaster loan.

text.p: The House voted Thursday to increase interest rates charged for disaster loans, just as Hurricane Fran was poised to strike southeastern states.
The disaster provision was in a bill, sent to the Senate on a 408-0 vote, to tighten up oversight and reduce the costs of Small Business Administration loans.
Disaster loans are used to help rebuild businesses in the wake of hurricanes, earthquakes, floods, fires and other catastrophes.

The current interest rate cap of 4 percent for many of the disaster loans would be increased to 7 percent. The loans are to be indexed at three-quarters the government's cost of borrowing money, which currently translates to roughly 5.25 percent for 10-year loans.
The measure also tightens up two of the most popular loan programs administered by the Small Business Administration.

Rep. Jan Meyers, a Kansas Republican who chairs the Small Business Committee, said the bill responded to problems with increased costs to the federal government. An aide said that was due to bad loans.

One plan, known as the "504" program, makes loans of $500,000 to $750,000 over seven to 10 years for most business purposes, a congressional aide said. The government guarantees 20 to 25 percent of the loans. About $10 billion annually in such loans are made.

The bill would restrict the number of lending institutions that can make such loans without extensive documentation. And, if congressional appropriators agree to provide extra money later, a database will be started to track loan performance.

The law would also increase fees for originating loans in another program, known as the "7(a)" program, which provides money for improvements in physical plants. About $2.5 billion to $3 billion in loans are made each year. Indidivudal loans are for similar amounts of those in the 504 program.
